raw.abstractText:
Background

Tibial transverse osteotomy (TTO) is a promising but limited surgical option for diabetic foot (DF). Berberine, a natural compound from Coptis chinensis, exhibits anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects relevant to metabolic diseases.

Objectives

This study aimed to evaluate whether adjunctive berberine enhances the therapeutic outcomes of TTO in DF patients and to explore its potential association with the platelet-derived growth factor-B (PDGF-B)/PDGF receptor-β (PDGFRβ) signaling pathway.

Methods

This was a prospective, single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, blinded trial. Of 200 screened DF patients, 96 eligible participants (Wagner grade 2-4) scheduled for TTO were randomized 1:1 to receive either TTO plus local berberine injections (n=48) or TTO plus local saline placebo (n=48). An additional non-randomized diabetic reference group (n=10) and healthy control group (n=10) were included for exploratory cellular studies only. The primary outcome was the total effective rate of ulcer healing at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included changes in Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI), ulcer area, Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score and serum inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6). Exploratory outcomes comprised serum VEGF, bFGF and PDGF-B levels, as well as fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue.

Results

All 96 randomized participants completed the 3-month follow-up, with no dropouts. The berberine group demonstrated a significantly higher total effective rate than the surgery-alone group (87.5% vs. 68.8%; risk difference, 18.7%; 95% CI, 1.2% to 36.2%; P < 0.05). At 3 months, the berberine group also showed greater improvements in ABI (mean difference, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.18; P < 0.01) and ulcer healing rate (mean difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 9.5% to 23.9%; P < 0.01), along with more significant reductions in hs-CRP and IL-6. Berberine treatment was associated with reduced fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue (mean difference, -1.10%; 95% CI, -1.56% to -0.64%; P = 0.001) and lower protein expression of PDGF-B and PDGFRβ. No severe adverse events related to berberine injections were reported.

Conclusion

In DF patients undergoing TTO, adjunctive local berberine therapy significantly improves the total effective rate and promotes ulcer healing, with benefits associated with reduced inflammation and fibroblast apoptosis and downregulation of the PDGF-B/PDGFRβ pathway. These findings are correlative and require further mechanistic validation. Larger multi-center trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety.

raw.abstractText: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent the first line of host immune defense against a broad spectrum of microorganisms. Whether naturally occurring or synthetically designed, these small peptides can potently inhibit microbial growth and remain stable under diverse conditions. Most AMPs act by directly disrupting fungal or bacterial membranes. In this study, we identified a glycine-rich peptide with strong antifungal activity against Botrytis cinerea. We further investigated its mode of action (MOA) and demonstrated its preventive antifungal activity in plants. Our work focuses primarily on the in vitro characterization of AMP features in the context of plant-Botrytis interactions.

raw.abstractText: Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) is a powerful reverse genetics tool that enables the transient knockdown of gene expression in plants by exploiting their natural antiviral defense mechanisms. This chapter presents a detailed protocol for applying a Cowpea severe mosaic virus (CPSMV)-based VIGS system to study gene function in soybean (Glycine max), with a focus on symbiotic root nodulation. VIGS allows systemic silencing of target genes, making it especially valuable to study pathways involving systemic signaling. The protocol includes Agrobacterium-mediated propagation of CPSMV variants in Nicotiana benthamiana, followed by mechanical inoculation of soybean plants and nodulation analysis. Detailed steps for vector construction, viral amplification, plant infection, and downstream molecular and phenotypic analyses are provided. This protocol is reproducible, accessible, and suitable for functional genomics studies in soybean, particularly for genes involved in nodulation but also in other developmental or stress-related processes.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Liver fibrosis is a chronic wound healing process of liver injury and gut-liver axis dysregulation has been recently identified as an important contributor to liver fibrosis progression. Quercetin has been reported to have anti-inflammatory activity and microbiota-modulating effects. However, the potential targets of quercetin remain unclear, as does the relationship between quercetin-associated targets and changes in the gut microbiota in liver fibrosis.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to use network pharmacology to predict potential targets of quercetin associated with liver fibrosis and to explore changes in gut microbiota following treatment with quercetin using a CCl4-induced rat model.

Methods

Eighteen male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into CON group, MOD group and QR group (n = 6 per group). Liver fibrosis was induced by weekly subcutaneous injection of carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) for eight weeks. Oral gavage of quercetin (50 mg/kg/day) was performed in QR group. Histopathological changes were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin staining, Masson staining and Ishak scoring. Potential targets of quercetin were screened using network pharmacology, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Cecal microbiota composition was determined by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Parametric or non-parametric tests were used accordingly, including one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test.

Results

Histopathology revealed significant liver injury and fibrosis in the MOD group relative to the CON group. The QR group showed lower Ishak fibrosis scores and milder histopathological features compared with the MOD group. Network pharmacology analysis identified UBC, UBE2I, RBX1, PSMB7 and UBA1 as hub targets, with KEGG pathways of interest including the TNF signaling pathway, p53 signaling pathway, Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. Alpha diversity of the cecal microbiota differed significantly among groups, whereas beta diversity did not. Relative abundance of Proteobacteria decreased and Firmicutes increased in the QR group relative to the MOD group. Taxa enrichment analysis identified enrichment of Muribaculaceae and Ligilactobacillus in the QR group.

Conclusion

Histopathology and microbiome analyses indicated that quercetin intervention was associated with altered liver histopathological features and shifts in gut microbiota composition in rats with CCl4-induced liver fibrosis. Network pharmacology predicted several hub targets and pathways potentially linked to these observations. As the present analyses are purely correlational and lack mechanistic validation at the molecular level, no causal relationships are implied between the predicted targets/pathways and the observed histological or microbiome changes. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant further validation studies.

raw.abstractText:
Background

 Fibrotic liver is one of the serious pathophysiological consequences of chronic injury to the liver, may progress toward serious complications including cirrhosis and hepatic carcinoma.

Objectives

Panax notoginseng is used for both therapeutic and prophylactic purposes in TCM; it is a source of Dencichine, an active substance that has been proven to exhibit antifibrotic properties in hepatic fibrosis. The present study investigated how Dencichine treatment ameliorates liver fibrosis using an animal model and a cellular fibrosis model.

Methods

Randomly assigned, male C57BL/6J mice received 10% CCl4 for 15 consecutive weeks to induce hepatic fibrosis. Treatment with Dencichine was initiated from 7th week onward. To simulate in-vitro the presence of a fibrotic microenvironment, LX-2 cells were treated with PDGF-BB at a concentration of 20 ng/mL and incubated from one up to four days and then treated by various doses of Dencichine. Liver function was evaluated by measuring alanine aminotransferase (ALT), AST, HA and LN. Histopathology was evaluated by haematoxylin/eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome and Sirius red stains. Quantitative real-time PCR and western blot analyses were used to evaluate mRNA and protein expression levels, respectively. Wound-healing assays and transwell chamber experiments were used to assess cell migration; EdU proliferation detection and flow cytometry were performed to measure cell proliferation and cell cycle, respectively.

Results

 The most important results are a considerable reduction of serum concentrations of AST and ALT, HA and laminin in CCl4-treated mice decreased liver injury and ECM deposition. Furthermore, this compound downregulated the expression of cyclin D1 and cyclin E1 and blocked the activation of PI3K and AKT kinases in fibrotic liver cells.

Conclusion

These results indicate that Dencichine may slow the development of liver fibrosis by interfering with the PI3K-AKT signaling cascade, demonstrating significant anti-scarring properties.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Ulcerative colitis is a relapsing inflammatory bowel disease driven by dysregulated immunity, epithelial barrier injury and microbial imbalance. Current therapies remain limited by relapse, adverse effects and incomplete response. Quercetin has anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective activities and ERK-MMP signaling may link inflammation to mucosal tissue damage.

Objectives

To evaluate whether the protective effects of quercetin in experimental ulcerative colitis (UC) are associated with modulation of ERK-MMP signaling, while avoiding causal overinterpretation beyond the animal and cellular evidence.

Methods

A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model and a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophage inflammatory model were used. Mice were allocated to the control, UC model and low-, medium- and high-dose quercetin groups. Disease activity index (DAI; unitless), colon length, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines and ERK/MMP-related molecules were evaluated by histological staining, ELISA, qRT-PCR and western blotting. In-vitro, quercetin was compared with the ERK phosphorylation inhibitor U0126 and an agonistic stimulus to explore pathway-related associations. The study was exploratory and did not include genetic rescue experiments or human validation.

Results

In DSS-treated mice, medium- and high-dose quercetin were associated with improved colon morphology, reduced DAI scores and partial restoration of colon length. Quercetin decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and increased IL-10 expression. In both mouse colon tissues and LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, quercetin was associated with reduced ERK1/2 activation and lower MMP-3 and MMP-9 expression, together with partial recovery of TIMP expression. These molecular changes were directionally consistent with the effects observed after ERK inhibition in-vitro.

Conclusion

Quercetin showed protective effects in experimental UC models and these effects may be associated with modulation of the ERK-MMP signaling axis. Further pathway-specific rescue experiments, pharmacokinetic studies and human-relevant models are required before this mechanism can be considered definitive or clinically translatable.

raw.abstractText: Shugan Formula (SGF) shows clinical hepatoprotective effects, but its mechanism against anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATB-DILI) remains unclear. This study employed LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics to investigate SGF's protective effects in rats. ATB-DILI was induced by oral isoniazid and rifampicin (100 mg·kg<sup>-1</sup> each) for 14 days. During modeling, the rats in the treated groups received low, medium, or high doses of SGF via oral gavage, whereas the PC group was administered obeticholic acid. Serum biomarkers (ALT, AST, IL-6, IL-10, and TNF-α), hepatic oxidative stress markers (MDA, SOD, GST, and GSH-Px), liver histopathology, and serum metabolomics were assessed. SGF treatment significantly reduced serum ALT, AST, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels, decreased hepatic MDA and GST levels, and increased SOD and GSH-Px activities. Metabolomics revealed that SGF attenuated metabolic perturbations induced by liver injury, with the high-dose group being most effective. Key pathways involved amino acid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and glycerophospholipid metabolism. This study provides scientific evidence for SGF in preventing and treating ATB-DILI.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Sarcopenia and frailty are frequent in patients with liver cirrhosis and are associated with morbidity and mortality. Given the limitations of computed tomography (CT) for routine assessment of muscle loss and the need for practical bedside assessment, we aimed to compare sonographic muscle thickness measurement and the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) for their prognostic value in patients with liver cirrhosis.

Methods

In this study, data of prospectively recruited patients with liver cirrhosis (both in- and outpatients) treated at a tertiary care centre were retrospectively analysed. Sonographic muscle thickness measurement was used to calculate the feather thigh muscle thickness index (fTMTI) and the compression thigh muscle thickness index (cTMTI). Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Patients were followed for liver transplantation or death.

Results

In total, 153 patients were included with a median Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) of 18 (Interquartile range (IQR) 10; 24). Ninety-five patients (62.0%) were male, and 70 patients (46%) were recruited in the outpatient setting. During the 90-day follow-up period, 71 patients (46.4%) either died or underwent liver transplantation. Outpatients had more muscle mass than inpatients and a lower CFS (fTMTI 19.1 mm/m vs. 12.1 mm/m, p < 0.001 and CFS 3 vs. 5, p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox-regression models adjusted for age and MELD score, a higher CFS remained independently associated with mortality and liver transplantation (LT) (HR 1.25 (1.14; 1.63), p < 0.001), whereas fTMTI and cTMTI were not consistently associated with a poorer prognosis (fTMTI HR 1.52 (0.68; 3.42), p = 0.300; cTMTI HR 1.01 (0.61; 1.68), p > 0.9). Subgroup analyses in men confirmed a superior prognostic value of CFS (HR 1.51 (1.17; 1.94), p = 0.001) over sonographic muscle thickness measurement (cTMTI HR 0.94 (0.84; 1.04), p = 0.200; fTMTI HR 0.93 (0.88; 1.00), p = 0.039).

Conclusion

CFS is robustly associated with poorer prognosis in patients with liver cirrhosis and seems to be superior to sonographic muscle thickness measurement of the thigh.

raw.abstractText: This study aimed to explore the processing mechanism of single medicinal herbs in compound prescriptions, compare the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic changes of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula before and after processing, and elucidate its underlying mechanism against gastric ulcers. The results showed that six components, namely, corydaline, coptisine chloride, palmatine, berberine chloride, phellopterin, and imperatorin, exerted anti-ulcer activities. The optimal vinegar-processing parameters for Corydalis yanhusuo were determined as follows: processing temperature of 84°C, vinegar dosage of 37%, and baking time of 35 min. Vinegar-processed Corydalis yanhusuo could accelerate the in vivo distribution of alkaloid components in the formula, elevate the plasma concentration, and prolong the in vivo retention time of coumarin components. The synergistic effects of the two types of active ingredients endow the vinegar-processed Yuanhu Zhitong Formula with significantly superior antigastric ulcer activity compared with the raw formula. Moreover, network pharmacology results revealed that this formula exerts therapeutic effects against gastric ulcers mainly by regulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This study clarified the optimal processing technology and the pharmacodynamic material basis of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula against gastric ulcers, confirmed the efficacy-enhancing effect of processing, and provided data support for the formulation of its processing production standards and clinical medication.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Caffeine is consumed for its presumed cognitive benefits, yet controlled studies have repeatedly failed to find effects on inhibitory control. Cross-sectional work suggests that people with elevated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms may benefit from chronic, moderate caffeine consumption, but whether acute intake improves cognition in proportion to symptom severity has not been tested experimentally.

Aims

We tested whether 250 mg of caffeine improves active inhibition (withholding a prepared response) and reactive inhibition (resolving response conflict), and whether ADHD symptom severity moderates these effects.

Methods

In a preregistered, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, a nonclinical sample of 36 young adults received 250 mg of caffeine or placebo in counterbalanced order, with testing 45 min after ingestion. Active inhibition was assessed with a Go/No-Go task (204 trials), reactive inhibition with an arrow flanker task (200 trials) and symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. Mixed-effects models included treatment, symptom severity, their interaction and ten covariates; Bayes factors quantified evidence for the null.

Results

Both tasks produced their benchmark effects (dz = 1.24 and 1.09) and all indices were reliable (split-half r = 0.73-0.98). Caffeine affected neither commission errors (BF01 = 4.98), response criterion (5.14), Go reaction time (2.83), reaction time variability (4.35), flanker reaction time (5.49) nor flanker accuracy (5.09). ADHD symptoms moderated no effect (15 preregistered tests; smallest p = 0.514), yet predicted performance itself (flanker accuracy r = -0.42), indicating that the null is not due to an insensitive measure.

Conclusions

Caffeine produced no acute benefit for either form of inhibition, and ADHD symptoms did not moderate its effects. Bayes factors supported the absence rather than the nondetection of these effects, arguing against an acute improvement of inhibitory control that scales with ADHD symptom severity in nonclinical young adults. Whether this also holds for chronic consumption or for adults with diagnosed ADHD remains to be tested.

raw.abstractText:
Objective

Caffeine could improve cognitive functions, but study protocols usually prohibit drinking coffee before cognitive testing. However, regular coffee consumers may experience withdrawal effects when they cannot drink their habitual coffee, which may impair cognitive performance. Therefore, we tested the effects of overnight coffee abstinence in regular coffee consumers: once allowing to drink their coffee and once not drinking coffee. The cognitive performance was compared with non-regular coffee consumers.

Methods

Thirty regular coffee consumers (RCCs) and 25 non-regular consumers (N-RCCs) took part in this study. RCCs were tested after their habitual morning coffee (c-RCC) and after overnight abstinence (a-RCC); N-RCCs were tested once. A cognitive battery assessed reaction time (RT), processing speed (digit symbol substitution test), working memory, verbal learning/memory and executive function (Stroop). Sleep quality was included as a covariate.

Results

Compared to c-RCC, overnight coffee abstinence significantly slowed RTs but did not affect the performance in the other cognitive tasks. In the a-RCC condition, but not the c-RCC condition, the RTs were slower than those of the N-RCCs, while accuracy measures were comparable across groups. Sleep quality did not alter these findings.

raw.abstractText: This study investigated the effects of 8 weeks of whey protein supplementation (30 g/day) on biomarkers of liver function, inflammation, and muscle damage in trained power-trained (predominantly speed-power/anaerobic-power disciplines) and endurance-trained athletes, in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design. Biomarkers assessed pre- and post-intervention included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), C-reactive protein (CRP), and creatine kinase (CK). Significant reductions in ALT, AST, and CK were observed in both endurance- and power-trained athletes after supplementation (p = 0.001, p = 0.015, p = 0.001, and p = 0.003 respectively), indicating attenuated hepatic and muscular stress. Among the four biomarkers, only ALT displayed a statistically significant three-way interaction (Time × Supplementation × Training modality; p = 0.003), identifying it as the sole marker showing a genuine modality-specific differential response to supplementation. A significant within-group reduction in CRP was additionally observed in the supplemented power-trained athletes (p = 0.039), whereas endurance athletes showed only minor, non-significant changes; because the omnibus three-way interaction for CRP was not significant, this finding is reported as a within-group trend rather than evidence of a differential effect between modalities. Placebo groups demonstrated stable or increased enzyme and CRP values, particularly in endurance athletes. These findings suggest that whey protein may attenuate exercise-induced hepatic and muscular stress across training modalities, with a modality-specific effect on hepatic stress markers (ALT) observed in power-trained athletes. The results highlight whey protein's potential as a nutritional aid to promote recovery and physiological adaptation, possibly mediated by antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Further studies are warranted to examine long-term outcomes and dose-response effects across different training profiles.

raw.abstractText: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N-H⋯OC hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together. (2S)-Proline (Pro) and (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline (Hyp) are enriched far above their proteome-wide abundance because they preorganize individual strands into the polyproline II conformation, lowering the entropic cost of folding. We asked whether the triple helix is intrinsically stable enough to form from strands that carry no such preorganization, that is, from polyglycine. To offset the conformational entropy of a Gly-rich tract, we embedded Gly<sub>6</sub> within flanking triple-helical (Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>n</sub> clamps in Ac-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>6</sub>-Gly<sub>6</sub>-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>5</sub>-Pro-Hyp-NH<sub>2</sub> and compared it with an otherwise identical peptide in which Gly<sub>6</sub> was replaced by two [2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethoxy]acetic acid units, a flexible, length-matched spacer that lacks most of the regularly spaced backbone amides of Gly<sub>6</sub>. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the diagnostic positive band at 225 nm. The molar ellipticity of the spacer-containing control was 86% of that of the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, matching the 35/41 = 85% ratio of residues capable of triple-helix formation and consistent with the Gly<sub>6</sub> segment contributing to the triple-helical signal. Thermal denaturation yielded a T<sub>m</sub> of 46.8°C for the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, 6.3°C higher than that of the matched spacer control. This added stability indicates that the polyglycine tract is not merely accommodated within the helix but contributes stabilizing interstrand hydrogen bonds. Together, these data indicate that three polyglycine strands can form a collagen triple helix when flanked by triple-helical clamps. This result is consistent with the idea that the triple-helical architecture predates the recruitment of Pro and Hyp, informs the evolutionary origin of collagen, and offers a blunt-ended, symmetric scaffold for designing peptidic triple helices.

While insulin activates the sympathetic nervous system in experimental settings, whether therapeutic insulin administration is associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance under free-living conditions remains unclear. This prospective observational study investigated the association between insulin dosing and cardiac autonomic balance in adults with type 1 diabetes managed exclusively with insulin therapy. Participants underwent continuous heart rate variability (HRV) and glucose monitoring over 4 consecutive days during routine daily activities. Cardiac sympathetic predominance was assessed using the low-frequency power to high-frequency power (LF/HF) ratio derived from HRV analysis, and associations were evaluated using generalized estimating equations. A higher last bolus insulin dose was associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the early sleep phase. A higher basal insulin dose was also associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the late sleep phase. These associations persisted after adjustment for mean glucose and mean absolute glucose change during the corresponding sleep phases. Under free-living conditions, higher insulin doses were associated with dose-dependent increases in cardiac sympathetic predominance, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing may be linked to cardiac autonomic regulation in individuals with type 1 diabetes, highlighting the importance of considering cardiac autonomic balance and potential cardiovascular risk when optimizing insulin therapy.

Article highlights

The relationship between therapeutic insulin administration and cardiac autonomic balance under free-living conditions remains unclear. We examined whether insulin dosing was associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance during daily life in adults with type 1 diabetes managed with insulin therapy. Higher last bolus and basal insulin doses were associated with increased cardiac sympathetic predominance during the early and late sleep phases, respectively, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing patterns may be linked to cardiac autonomic balance, with potential implications for optimizing insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes.

Background

Prolonged exposure to hepatotoxic antiretroviral therapy (ART) could lead to chronic liver injury, which might increase risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We used causal inference methods to evaluate if cumulative exposure to ART with known mechanisms of chronic liver injury is associated with HCC among people with HIV (PWH), by chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of antiretroviral-naive PWH with and without diagnosed CLD who initiated ART in the Veterans Affairs between 1999 and 2023. Exposure to ART with known mechanism of chronic liver injury (mitochondrial toxicity or accumulation of toxic intermediates) was determined monthly through prescription fills. Incident HCC was identified by Veterans Affairs National Cancer Registry and/or recorded diagnoses. Marginal structural models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of HCC associated with cumulative exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART compared with ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms, by CLD status.

Results

Among 11,854 PWH without CLD and 6771 PWH with CLD, we observed 112 and 378 HCC events, respectively. Among PWH without CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was associated with HCC when compared with ≥4 years of use of ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms (OR = 4.02 [95% CI: 1.00-16.24]). Among PWH with CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was not associated with HCC (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.68-2.72).

Conclusion

Four or more years of ART with a chronic liver injury mechanism was associated with HCC among PWH without CLD, but not those with CLD.

Purpose

To investigate the microbial species latent in corneas of healthy individuals and determine whether small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) serves as a risk factor for pathogen reactivation.

Setting

Ophthalmology Department of Peking University Third Hospital, Beijing, China.

Design

Prospective cohort study.

Methods

Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was used to analyze the microbial composition of corneal lenticules from SMILE. Based on the results, patients were categorized into viral group (VG) and nonviral pathogen group (NVPG). 2 Matched groups (MG1 and MG2) were established by selecting pathogen-negative individuals at a 1:4 ratio relative to 2 positive groups. Using SPSS to analyze baseline characteristics, preoperative ocular parameters, and postoperative ocular parameters among groups.

Among the detected pathogens, latent Herpesviruses were identified in 9 cases (4.31%), Papillomavirus were 4 cases (1.91%), and nonviral pathogens were 20 cases (9.57%). Both VG and NVPG groups showed no significant differences in baseline characteristics or preoperative ocular parameters compared with MG groups. In postoperative ocular parameters, no significant differences were found between VG and MG1, although intergroup variations in intraocular pressure and corneal thickness were observed ( P > .05). However, NVPG demonstrated significantly poorer results than MG2 in 1-month spherical equivalent ( P = .033) and corneal epithelial staining ( P = .044).

Conclusions

These findings indicate pathogen latency does not affect ocular status and SMILE surgery is unlikely to reactivate latent viruses or exerts minimal influence. Viral latency has almost no impact on postoperative recovery, while latent nonviral pathogens may interfere with postoperative recovery.

raw.abstractText: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. Although endogenous NE is known to stimulate MEL synthesis, the effects of exogenous intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentration, particularly under general anaesthesia (GA), remain poorly characterised. This study examined the influence of intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentrations in healthy volunteers, both awake and under general anaesthesia. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. Background

Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. Despite growing scientific interest, no bibliometric study has systematically mapped the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this field.

Aim

To analyse the bibliometric characteristics and thematic structure of publications on sleep deprivation, sleep promotion and sleep quality in ICU patients indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 1983 and 2026.

Study design

A descriptive and evaluative bibliometric analysis was conducted. Data were retrieved on April 26, 2026, from the WoS Core Collection using a comprehensive search strategy. Publications were filtered by document type, WoS categories (nursing, critical care medicine, anaesthesiology) and index (SCI-EXPANDED, SSCI, ESCI). Data were analysed using R software with the Biblioshiny interface, and annual publication trends were evaluated using Microsoft Excel.

Results

Of 11 418 publications retrieved, 379 met the inclusion criteria, spanning 37 years (1983-2026). Linear regression revealed a statistically significant positive trend in publication output (β = 0.643, R2 = 0.704, r = 0.839, p < 0.001), with mean annual publications of 10.24 ± 8.83 and notable acceleration from the 2000s onwards. Thematic mapping identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation' and 'delirium' as motor themes both highly central and well developed. Emerging concepts included circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain and anxiety.

Conclusions

ICU sleep research has grown substantially over four decades, with sleep deprivation and delirium emerging as co-dominant research priorities. Thematic gaps and emerging clusters identified in this analysis highlight important directions for future nursing research and evidence-based practice development in critical care.

Relevance to clinical practice

This bibliometric analysis identified sleep deprivation and delirium as the co-dominant motor themes of ICU sleep research, and intervention-related concepts such as earplugs, eye masks and melatonin as emerging clusters. These evidence-based trends can guide ICU nurses in prioritizing targeted sleep promotion protocols and support policymakers in directing resources toward the most scientifically mature intervention areas in critical care.

Original ELISA spreadsheets provided 26 controls, 29 evaluable drug-naïve participants and 32 methylphenidate-treated participants. α-Synuclein differed among groups (H = 49.859, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.570), with all pairwise contrasts significant. Serum α-synuclein and total tau showed distinct cross-sectional group patterns. These associations do not establish methylphenidate effects and require prospective confirmation.

raw.abstractText: TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK, the TAM receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), play roles in phagocytosis and negative regulation of immune responses, contributing to homeostasis in many adult tissues. Aberrant TAM signaling leads to diseases including autoimmune disorders, viral infection, inflammation, and cancer. Development of successful drugs targeting TAM receptors is hindered by incomplete knowledge of the receptor activation mechanism. Receptor dimerization is assumed to play a role, as seen for most RTKs. However, full biological responses require the TAM ligands to engage phosphatidylserine in an opposing cell or virus membrane, suggesting a more complex mechanism, possibly involving higher-order receptor oligomerization or clustering. Here, we present an X-ray crystal structure of the ectodomain of MERTK, which adopts a highly curved conformation with key interdomain boundaries stabilized by N-linked glycan moieties. We show that this MERTK extracellular region (ECR) forms a similar conformation in solution using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), which also suggests a flexible ECR. We compare these crystallographic and solution data for MERTK with SAXS and AlphaFold structural predictions for the other two TAM receptors. SAXS data confirm that each TAM ECR has a distinct curvature, with TYRO3 the most bent and AXL relatively straight. This leads us to speculate that these different ectodomain conformations guide receptor-specific functions. The MERTK X-ray crystal structure also suggests a head-to-tail intermolecular interaction between the Ig2 domain of one MERTK and the FNIIIb domain of a second that has intriguing parallels with interactions that have been proposed to regulate Eph receptor clustering.

raw.abstractText: Activity-guided separation of medicinal plants requires linking activity signals and chromatographic resolution in complex matrices. In this study, based on a previously established HPLC-DPPH platform, medium-pressure prefractionation and preparative chromatographic purification were applied for the targeted isolation of free radical scavengers from Saxifraga tangutica (S. tangutica). raw.abstractText: Ripened washed-rind and long-ripened cheeses owe their prized sulfurous, savory character to intensive proteolysis and amino-acid catabolism; the same activity, when poorly controlled, also generates sensory off-flavors and toxic biogenic amines (BAs). Histamine and tyramine reach up to approximately 2000-2500 and 1000-2000 mg/kg in extreme samples, although most cheeses contain far less, so that a 30-g portion of a high-histamine cheese can exceed the 50-mg per-meal intake regarded as without adverse effect in healthy adults. Flavor formation and chemical safety have traditionally been studied apart. This critical review reframes them as two outcomes of one metabolism: Proteolysis liberates a shared free amino-acid pool from which volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs) and BAs arise. Because the principal VSCs derive from methionine whereas the major BAs derive from histidine, tyrosine, ornithine, arginine, and lysine, we treat the branches not as direct competitors for one substrate but as metabolically coupled fates linked by shared proteolytic supply, overlapping physicochemical controls and microbial cross-feeding. Integrating evidence across cheese families, we reclassify the ripening microbiota into condition-dependent functional guilds, formalize metabolic bivalence (organisms that both generate flavor and degrade amines), and define a sensory inflection point separating the windowed VSC dose-response from the monotonic BA hazard. We critically appraise multi-omics, volatilomics, biosensors, machine learning, and digital twins, and outline a precision-fermentation roadmap. Current, largely in vitro, and single-variety evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, controllable decoupling, which we frame as a testable hypothesis that recasts cheese quality as a controllable metabolic-allocation problem.

raw.abstractText: Prosthetic heart valve development consists of several branching, innovative strategies to mediate the complex native environment that wears down valve durability. Anti-calcification treatments are being applied to pericardial tissue, durable polymers are being developed that mitigate oxidative degradation and stress cracking, and heart valve tissue engineering has introduced resorbable scaffolds that can develop into stable, functional tissue. In each case, an increasing breadth of strategies is being developed to curb the persistent issue of valve deterioration. This study aimed to synthesize and characterize an ascorbic acid-containing polyurethane to impart antioxidant properties to degradable scaffolds for tissue engineered heart valve (TEHV) replacement. Blends of poly(carbonate-ascorbic acid) urethane (PCAU) and poly(carbonate urethane) urea (PCUU) were fabricated into microporous scaffolds to evaluate the impact of PCAU in vitro on mechanics, degradation, cell viability, calcification, bacterial adhesion, and in vivo on native tissue response in a juvenile rat subcutaneous model. PCAU blended with PCUU in a 25:75 ratio (PCAU-25) had mechanical properties similar to PCUU, while higher concentrations of PCAU were not mechanically robust. PCAU-25 showed greater reactive oxygen species (ROS) inhibition and degradation, and reduced calcification and bacterial adhesion in vitro. In a juvenile rat subcutaneous model, both PCUU and PCAU-25 groups showed negligible calcification after 4 weeks. PCAU-25, however, showed much greater cell infiltration and immune response, possibly due to an accelerated rate of degradation. PCAU-25 was then fabricated into a polymeric valve scaffold and underwent basic mechanical and hydrodynamic performance assessment that demonstrated function similar to PCUU valves previously reported. These findings demonstrate proof-of-concept for a new polyurethane formulation incorporating ascorbic acid for antioxidant bioactivity and translatability into a functional TEHV scaffold.

raw.abstractText: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

raw.abstractText:
Background

The results of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) regarding the effect of vitamin D supplementation on mortality reduction are conflicting.

Objective

The aim of this study was to assess the level of evidence through a sensitivity analysis of the meta-analysis by Shah et al. (2024) using the Rebuilt the Evidence Base (REB) method.

Methods

The main inclusion criterion was a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT design. The exclusion criteria were trials combining vitamin D with other nutrients and unpublished RCTs. The main outcome was all-cause mortality. A bias analysis was performed, followed by a hypothetico-deductive analysis to determine the confirmatory or exploratory nature of each RCT. The REB method was used to interpret the results and assess the level of evidence.

Results

Among the 25 RCTs included in the meta-analysis by Shah et al., the analysis was performed on 8 RCTs at low risk of bias including 30 320 participants. Seven RCTs raised some concerns, and two RCTs were at high risk of bias according to ROB2. Bias arose from the randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and selection of the reported results. The results were statistically significant, in favor of vitamin D supplementation: RR = 0.96 (95% CI [0.92, 1.00]), p = 0.04. No RCT was conclusive.

Conclusion

According to the REB method, there is an evidence signal regarding the benefit of vitamin D supplementation in the population aged 75 and older, which remains to be confirmed.

raw.abstractText: As polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) durability targets continue to increase, rapid and reliable evaluation of stack durability becomes increasingly important. Conventional catalyst accelerated stress test (AST) methods are primarily designed for single-cell evaluation using a potentiostat, limiting their direct application to stacks. In this study, a catalyst AST method applicable to stacks is investigated using load cycling. A three-cell stack is subjected to four durability protocols with different voltage ranges, operating temperatures, and oxidants, and the resulting performance and catalyst degradation are evaluated. Increasing the operating temperature by 10°C accelerates the performance degradation rate by 36%. The use of oxygen as the oxidant with an increased upper potential further accelerates the degradation rate by 85%. When the temperature increases by 10°C, oxygen is used as the oxidant, and both the upper and lower potential limits are extended, the degradation rate increases by more than twofold. These results indicate that Pt oxidation promoted by increased oxidant concentration and upper potential, together with Pt dissolution associated with the applied potential range, plays an important role in accelerating catalyst degradation. The proposed load-based AST provides a practical approach for rapid catalyst durability evaluation at the PEMFC stack level.

raw.abstractText: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, yet its molecular determinants remain difficult to characterize in real-world settings, as genomic and clinical data are fragmented across resources. Existing databases typically separate gene-level mechanisms, curated genotype-phenotype associations, and large-scale clinical antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) data, limiting cross-scale interpretation. Here, we present Omni-ARMD, an open-access knowledgebase that integrates multi-source genomic and clinical data to systematically infer genotype-phenotype relationships in AMR. Omni-ARMD bridges large-scale clinical AST records and gene-level resistance evidence through a confidence-weighted log-odds enrichment framework, which quantifies genotype-phenotype associations at the organism-antimicrobial level and integrates these associations into aggregated cross-domain evidence representations. The current release includes over 12 million de-identified microbiology records from more than 1 million patients, harmonized to generate over 7.83 million standardized AST records. It also integrates over 0.36 million gene-phenotype associations, spanning 38 organisms, 52 antimicrobials, and 375 resistance genes. Omni-ARMD links over 5.16 million clinical records to genomic evidence, achieving a 65.86% match rate and a 2.61% coverage of organism-antimicrobial pairs. Omni-ARMD provides interactive modules for clinical investigation, genomic evidence analysis, mechanistic interpretation, and artificial intelligence-assisted exploration, enabling integrative and data-driven discovery in AMR. Omni-ARMD is freely available at www.omniarmd.cn.

raw.title: The Bias Continuum Framework (BCF) for Medicine–Food Homology: A Derivable Operational Scale across Food, Food-Medicine, and Medicine
raw.authorString: Yang G.
raw.abstractText: Objective The current Chinese catalogue of medicinal and edible substances applies a "safety–history" criterion that decides whether a substance may be admitted, but it cannot state how strong its cold–hot nature bias is after admission, where its boundaries lie relative to everyday foods and medicines, or how it should be used according to individual constitution. This study constructs an operational scoring framework that uses cold–hot nature bias as a single coordinate axis, is fully rule-disclosed and reproducibly computable, and can be extrapolated to plant-derived substances that lie outside the frozen reference tables. Methods We propose the Bias Continuum Framework (BCF; methodological framework V1), in which foods and medicines are defined as intervals on a continuum of [− 10, + 10], indexed by the nature bias score B (positive = warm/hot, negative = cool/cold, zero = neutral). B is computed from three measurable dimensions—environmental habits (40%), metabolic characteristics (40%), and growth cycle (20%)—under a publicly specified operational scoring rule. Two cut-offs partition the continuum into three zones: |B|≤3, the low-bias (food-nourishment dominant) zone; 3<|B|≤6, the moderate-bias (medicine–food homology) zone; and |B|>6, the high-bias (medicine dominant) zone. The three-dimensional rules and weights were frozen and published on an international preprint platform in 2025, and no rule was retroactively changed for any substance in the present calibration. The 106 national catalogue substances were scored item by item and reported by evidence tier (L1/L2/L3a/L3b/R). Validation followed an ascending staircase: in-system consistency (60 typical foods/herbs), extrapolation of the frozen rules to 19 off-catalogue foodstuffs, and a "predict-before-check" blind prediction on 15 exotic crops and new-resource foods outside the reference tables, supplemented by a cut-off grid sensitivity analysis. Results The 106 substances were classified as 41 low-bias (38.7%), 50 moderate-bias (47.2%), and 15 high-bias (14.2%), a unimodal distribution that bulges in the middle and tapers at both ends. All 30 everyday foods fell in the low-bias zone, and 28 of 30 recognised strongly biased herbs fell in the high-bias zone, with zero food–medicine diagonal misclassification. Of the 19 off-catalogue foodstuffs, 17 were low-bias and 2 (winter melon B = − 3.2, bitter melon B = − 3.3) crossed into the lower edge of the moderate-bias zone. The three-zone structure remained stable for α∈[2.5, 3.5] and β∈[5.5, 6.5]. B correlated strongly with the rank of Pharmacopoeia natures (Spearman ρ = 0.910, n = 106, P < 0.001; ρ = 0.938 in the high-confidence subset), and the plant-derived score span within a single Pharmacopoeia nature label reached about 6.9 points (the four natures govern direction rather than intensity). All 15 high-bias substances were supported by high-confidence evidence (L1/L2); a leave-one-class-out sensitivity analysis that removed all L3b and animal-source (R) entries left the high-bias membership unchanged (0% change). In the blind prediction, 13 of 15 exotic crops agreed in cold–hot direction with public reports; the two exceptions (guarana, cacao) were both rich in caffeine and theobromine (excitatory methylxanthines), precisely exposing a coverage gap of the frozen rule in the metabolic dimension. None of the 15 fell in the high-bias zone, reproducing the general pattern that everyday foods cluster in the low-bias zone. Conclusions The BCF is a reproducible, calibratable, and extrapolatable operational scoring tool that complements rather than replaces the current catalogue: the catalogue governs legality and safety (whether a substance may be admitted or traded), whereas the continuum governs cold–hot displacement and adaptation constraints (how it should be used by constitution, dose, and frequency). The B score measures the direction and intensity of cold–hot bias and is not a direct measure of therapeutic efficacy or toxicity. Because its three-dimensional inputs are botanical measurable parameters independent of classical texts, the framework is, by design, able to compute cold–hot direction and zone membership for exotic crops and new-resource foods "for which botanical data exist but no classical textual record does"; until independent-criterion validation is completed, such results remain "values computed under the frozen rules." The two blind-prediction reversals (the methylxanthine gap) constitute preliminary evidence of the framework's falsifiability. Independent-scorer blind replication (inter-rater reliability) and modern pharmacological criterion association have been registered as subsequent validations.

raw.authorString: Prakash R, K R, Reghukumar A.
raw.abstractText: Background Acanthamoeba brain infection can cause ring-enhancing lesions that mimic neoplasm, abscess or demyelination on brain imaging. High-dose corticosteroids, the standard treatment for tumefactive demyelination, can be detrimental if infection is not systematically excluded. Case presentation: A 42-year-old immunocompetent woman presented with a two-week history of non-fluent aphasia, executive dysfunction, and progressive right hemiparesis. An MRI scan of the brain showed two left frontoparietal lesions with perilesional oedema, open-ring enhancement, and mass effect. Spectroscopy showed elevated choline and reduced N-acetyl aspartate. Based on the radiological differential diagnosis of tumefactive demyelination versus high-grade glioma, intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g daily was initiated at an outside hospital before referral to our centre. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) study on day 5 of methylprednisolone showed 6 cells/mm³, sugar 78 mg/dL, protein 79 mg/dL, and no oligoclonal bands. CSF 18S rRNA PCR detected Acanthamoeba spp. Combination anti-acanthamoeba therapy (doxycycline, fluconazole, co-trimoxazole, and miltefosine) was administered. The lesions regressed, and deficits improved; however, CSF Acanthamoeba PCR remained positive even after four months of treatment, with co-detection of parvovirus B19. Conclusion Acanthamoeba CNS infection can mimic the clinical, neuroradiological, and spectroscopic features of tumefactive demyelination, including the characteristic open-ring sign. When tumefactive lesions lack definitive features of established demyelinating disease, it is prudent to rule out infective etiologies, such as CNS infections with free-living amoebae, before administering immunomodulators.

raw.abstractText:
Background/aims

Cell-membrane gasdermin D (GSDMD) plays a key role as a pyroptosis executor of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). However, the mitochondrial translocation of GSDMD occurs even during the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver (MASL) phase, which involves mainly hepatic steatosis without tremendous inflammatory responses or sustainable hepatic cell death; the underlying mechanism is unknown. We investigated the role of GSDMD in the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

Methods

Liver tissues from patients with MASLD and control subjects were obtained to evaluate GSDMD expression and distribution. GSDMD△hep mice and their floxed littermate controls, GSDMDfl/fl mice, were fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet (HFHCD) for 4 and 12 weeks to develop MASL or MASH, respectively. Additionally, GSDMD△hep mice were administered an adeno-associated virus 8 (AAV8) vector expressing wild-type GSDMD (GSDMD-WT) or GSDMD O-GlcNAcylation site mutants (GSDMD-T174/S178A) and were provided with an HFHCD or a methionine-choline-deficient diet.

Results

GSDMD expression and mitochondrial translocation were increased in patients and experimental mice with MASLD. The translocation of GSDMD-NT to mitochondria impaired the mitochondrial membrane potential and promoted the leakage of cytochrome c and mitochondrial DNA, thus inducing early hepatocyte apoptosis, and was required for pyroptosis in MASLD. O-GlcNAcylation at T173/T175 (in humans) or T174/S178 (in mice) of GSDMD was responsible for GSDMD mitochondrial translocation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Targeting O-GlcNAcylation with Celecoxib suppressed GSDMD mitochondrial translocation and the development of MASLD.

Conclusions

Targeting mitochondrial GSDMD-mediated programed cell death (PCD) pathways may provide new insights into the potential theoretical basis for MASLD interventions.

raw.abstractText: Regulatory changes enacted through the 2018 Agriculture Improvement Act established the distinction between legal hemp and illicit marijuana based on a 0.3% Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ9-THC) dry-weight threshold, reshaping analytical requirements for forensic laboratories. The influx of cannabis submissions and the quantitative requirements for marijuana identification have contributed to controlled substance backlogs and operational strain, prompting the adoption of more conservative semi-quantitative 1% decision-point methodologies. Differentiating hemp and marijuana is further complicated by the isomeric nature of Δ9-THC and cannabidiol (CBD), often requiring time-intensive chromatographic methods, including gas chromatography and liquid chromatography. This study provides a rapid, direct mass spectrometry approach for marijuana identification using copper-phosphine ion complexation and commercialized paper spray ionization-mass spectrometry (PSI-MS). Thirteen cannabinoids and a deuterated internal standard, Δ9-THC-d9, were characterized in the presence of [Cu(PPh3)2(ACN)2]BF4, generating characteristic copper-bound, oxidized cannabinoid species. A [Cu+2PPh3+Δ9-THC+O-2H]+ complex was observed at m/z 915, whereas CBD did not form an observable complex, thereby eliminating CBD interference for Δ9-THC quantitation. A semi-quantitative 1% decision-point assay was established by fortifying cannabis samples with Δ9-THC-d9 at a 1% administrative threshold and determining whether the post-decarboxylation Δ9-THC content exceeds the 1% administrative threshold. Validation studies established selectivity, accuracy, precision, expanded uncertainty, carryover, and limit of detection. The validated method was applied to methanolic extracts of 36 decarboxylated authentic cannabis samples, resulting in a 94% corrected identification rate, with two misidentifications due to high cannabinol (CBN) concentrations. The developed method enables marijuana identification in approximately 4 minutes, enhancing laboratory throughput and potentially minimizing casework backlogs.

raw.authorString: Eun S, Jeong E, Chae S, Lee S.
raw.abstractText:
Background:

/Objectives: The separate contributions of excess energy intake and diet composition to high-fat diet (HFD)-induced adiposity, adipose inflammation, and gut microbial changes are unclear. We tested whether restricting HFD intake to the energy intake of low-fat (LF)-fed mice (isocaloric restriction) prevents or reverses these outcomes. Subjects/Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice (n = 8/group) received for 12 weeks an LF diet (LF/LF) or HFD (HF/HF) ad libitum, HFD ad libitum then isocaloric HFD from week 7 (HF/IHF), or isocaloric HFD throughout (IHF/IHF). Adiposity, plasma markers, adipose and ileal gene expression, and fecal microbiota (16S rRNA sequencing, n = 4/group) were assessed.

Results:

Final body weight in IHF/IHF did not differ from LF/LF (difference 0.1 g, 95% CI -6.5 to 6.7; P > 0.99) and was lower than in HF/HF (-8.2 g, -14.7 to -1.6; P = 0.011). Switching to isocaloric feeding reduced weight gain during weeks 6-12 (HF/IHF vs HF/HF, -6.4 g, -9.8 to -3.1; P < 0.001). IHF/IHF mice had lower glucose (P = 0.031) and cholesterol (P = 0.005) than HF/HF mice. However, visceral fat relative to body weight remained higher than in LF/LF in IHF/IHF (+1.5 percentage points, 0.04 to 2.9; P = 0.042) and HF/IHF (+1.8, 0.4 to 3.3; P = 0.008). Adipose Tnf expression remained elevated in HF/IHF (log2 difference 2.2, 0.2 to 4.2; P = 0.025), and fecal phylogenetic diversity was lower in IHF/IHF than in LF/LF (Faith's PD -3.1, -5.9 to -0.4; P = 0.024). Ileal barrier genes and plasma lipopolysaccharide-binding protein were unchanged.

Conclusions:

Limiting HFD energy intake normalized body weight, glycemia, and plasma lipids but not relative adiposity, adipose Tnf expression, or the loss of gut microbial diversity. Diet composition affects these outcomes independently of energy intake, so normal body weight does not indicate their reversal.

raw.abstractText: Developing phosphite-based birefringent materials with simultaneously large birefringence and wide optical transparency remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the large intrinsic polarizability anisotropy of planar π-conjugated ligands, we introduced 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) into the magnesium phosphite system to explore the influence of ligand packing on birefringence. Colorless crystals of Mg(phen)(HPO3) (1) and Mg(phen)(H2PO3)2·H2O (2) were successfully obtained under different solvothermal conditions. Although both compounds crystallize in the same monoclinic space group C2/c and consist of one-dimensional magnesium phosphite chains, they exhibit markedly different packing arrangements of the phen ligands. In compound 1, adjacent phen ligands are nearly perpendicular with a dihedral angle of approximately 90°, resulting in a birefringence of 0.36 at 546 nm. In contrast, compound 2 features a nearly parallel packing of the phen ligands and exhibits a remarkably large birefringence of 0.55 at 546 nm, placing it among the most birefringent phosphite-based materials reported to date. Theoretical calculations reveal that the birefringence is dominated by the π-conjugated phen ligands, while the phosphite groups make a much smaller contribution. These findings demonstrate that regulating the packing mode of π-conjugated ligands is an effective approach to enhancing birefringence in metal phosphite hybrids.

raw.abstractText:
Study Objectives: The causal effects of daylight exposure on sleep remain poorly understood, particularly under real-world conditions. This study aimed to address this gap by examining the effects of an afternoon daylight intervention on subsequent sleep.

Methods:

Ten healthy participants (4 males; 19 to 28 years) completed two randomized 3-h afternoon outdoor walks under high-intensity light (HIL; clear goggles) or attenuated light (AL; neutral-density-filtered goggles; ~10 photopic lux) conditions. Light exposure was centered around the estimated crossover between the phase-advancing and phase-delaying portions of the light phase-response curve, individually determined from baseline dim light melatonin onset (DLMO). Subsequent nocturnal sleep was assessed using at-home polysomnography (PSG), and subjective sleepiness and sleep quality were assessed using the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale and Groningen Sleep Quality Scale, respectively. Differences between conditions and across time were examined using linear mixed-effects models.

Results:

There were no significant differences between conditions in DLMO timing or the phase angle between DLMO and sleep onset, indicating that the light manipulation did not produce a detectable shift in circadian phase. Sleep duration and self-reported sleep quality were also unchanged. However, nighttime delta power accumulated more rapidly following HIL exposure, accompanied by greater NREM sleep and reduced wakefulness after sleep onset (all p < 0.01). Participants were also significantly less sleepy upon awakening following HIL compared with AL exposure (p < 0.05).

Conclusions:

High-intensity natural daylight exposure may promote greater sleep intensity and reduce sleepiness upon awakening. These findings highlight a potential role for daytime light exposure in modulating subsequent sleep physiology and next-morning sleepiness, independent of changes in circadian phase.

Purpose

This systematic review evaluates the relationship between classical psychedelic drugs (D-Lysergic acid N,N-diethylamide, psilocybin, ayahuasca/N-N-dimethyl-tryptamine, and mescaline) and the emergence of psychotic symptoms, aiming to synthesize evidence from contemporary studies (1984-2025) regarding the risk factors, prevalence, and clinical characteristics of psychosis related to psychedelic use, to provide clinicians, therapists, and policymakers with a framework for identifying and mitigating risks related to these substances.

Major findings

Fifty-two papers were included, comprising 1 larger-scale studies involving over 100,000 individuals and 34 case reports. Population-based data showed no consistent correlation between lifetime psychedelic use and psychosis. Controlled clinical settings showed minimal risk, with one documented case of transient delusions across all trials. Emergency and toxicological data reported higher rates of psychotic symptoms, likely reflecting the severity of cases prompting medical attention. Among case reports, 58% of individuals had a personal or family psychiatric history. First-episode psychosis, although rare, was documented in otherwise healthy individuals.

Conclusions

The risk of prolonged psychosis remains remarkably low in controlled clinical settings where rigorous screening and supervision are employed. Personal/family history of psychosis and unsupervised, naturalistic use appear to be risk factors for psychosis. Although causality remains difficult to establish, these findings support the need for careful risk stratification, the adoption of clear diagnostic parameters, and trained clinical oversight as psychedelic-assisted therapies advance toward broader clinical populations.

Purpose of review

Pharmacotherapy is widely used to manage neuropsychiatric sequelae that may interfere with neurorehabilitation after traumatic brain injury (TBI), despite limited TBI-specific evidence. This review summarizes psychopharmacological evidence from the past 18 months and proposes a three-step approach: deprescribing potentially recovery-limiting medications, characterizing individual neuropsychiatric symptoms, and selecting symptom-targeted treatments to support cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and functional recovery after TBI.

Recent findings

Methylphenidate shows the most consistent evidence for selected cognitive outcomes, particularly attention and processing speed. Pharmacological approaches to agitation, sleep-wake disorders, depression, fatigue, and posttraumatic headache have been studied, but TBI-specific evidence remains limited or heterogeneous. Sedative, anticholinergic, and cognitive adverse effects, cardiovascular risks, and dependence require consideration in TBI neurorehabilitation.

Summary

No pharmacological treatment is established as disease-modifying after TBI. Given the limited evidence, psychopharmacotherapy should be individualized, symptom-targeted, and integrated into multidisciplinary TBI neurorehabilitation. Continuous medication review and deprescribing should accompany careful treatment selection and monitoring. Future trials should determine whether symptom improvement translates into better rehabilitation participation, functional independence, and long-term health-related quality of life.

raw.abstractText: Estuarine microbiomes are rich ecological niches for discovering novel secondary metabolites with therapeutic applications. This study focuses on the isolation, purification, structural elucidation, and antineoplastic evaluation of a red pigment from a marine microbial isolate. The bacterium Zooshikella sp. RANM57 was isolated from the Netravathi River estuary. Biomass was recovered using an alum-induced flocculation technique and solvent extraction, after which the primary pigment was purified via flash chromatography and structurally characterized using HRLCMS-QTOF and NMR spectroscopy. Anticancer potential was evaluated against human PC-3 prostate cancer cells using MTT and clonogenic assays. The underlying apoptotic mechanism was delineated using Annexin V/PI staining, Caspase-3 quantification, and TUNEL assays. The purified pigment was identified as the tripyrrole alkaloid heptyl prodigiosin based on HRLCMS-QTOF, UV-Vis/FT-IR profiling, and 1D NMR spectral concordance with reported prodiginine features. In vitro evaluations revealed significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity against PC-3 cells (IC 50  = 9.00 µg/mL), demonstrating high anticancer efficacy relative to cisplatin. Mechanistic profiling confirmed that cell death occurred exclusively via an intrinsic apoptotic cascade, as evidenced by significant phosphatidylserine externalization (17.60%), executioner Caspase-3 activation (52.45%), and terminal DNA fragmentation (21.25%), without inducing primary necrosis. Furthermore, treatment also reduced clonogenic survival after 24 h exposure and 8-day outgrowth. The successful isolation and characterization of heptyl prodigiosin from Zooshikella sp. RANM57 underscores the value of estuarine bacteria in natural product discovery. Our biological evaluations demonstrate that the compound functions as a precise, potent inducer of caspase-associated apoptosis, positioning this tripyrrole scaffold as a highly promising candidate for further anticancer pharmacological development.

raw.abstractText: SUMMARYSpecies of several mushroom genera, among them Psilocybe and Inocybe, biosynthesize psilocybin, the prodrug to the powerful psychotropic and perception-altering analog, psilocin. While "magic" mushrooms are popular as recreational drugs, advanced clinical trials have shown that psilocybin is a valuable future (and, in some countries, available) medication against depression and anxiety. In this review article, we focus on the metabolic processes leading to psilocybin in the fungal cell and present the biosynthetic enzymes, their structures, and the reactions catalyzed. Remarkably, mushrooms have evolved psilocybin biosynthesis twice independently, involving genes and enzymes that are only distantly related or unrelated altogether. We also present routes on how this iconic natural product can be made biocatalytically in vitro or in heterologous hosts in vivo. Despite substantial progress in psilocybin research over the past decade, we present unsolved questions that remain for the current and the next generation of researchers.

raw.abstractText: Study Design : Controlled experimental animal study. Objectives : To investigate the effect of four weeks of aerobic treadmill training combined with resveratrol supplementation on spinal cord interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) levels and locomotor recovery in a rat model of spinal cord injury (SCI). Setting : University-based exercise physiology and animal research laboratory, Bojnourd, Iran. Methods : Thirty-six male Wistar rats were allocated to healthy, SCI-control, resveratrol, exercise, and resveratrol + exercise groups. SCI was induced via a standardized weight-drop contusion at T10, and, beginning 14 days post-injury, rats underwent 4 weeks of body-weight-supported treadmill training and/or daily intraperitoneal resveratrol (10 mg/kg). Locomotor recovery was assessed using the Basso-Beattie-Bresnahan (BBB) scale, and spinal cord IL-6 and TNF-α levels were measured by ELISA. Results : SCI significantly elevated spinal cord IL-6 and TNF-α relative to healthy controls (P < 0.05). Resveratrol supplementation, alone and combined with exercise, significantly reduced spinal cord IL-6 relative to control, whereas exercise alone did not. The combined resveratrol + exercise group showed the most consistent anti-inflammatory profile, with significantly lower IL-6 than the exercise-alone group, and was the only intervention group with significantly reduced TNF-α. BBB scores improved significantly only in the exercise-containing groups. Conclusions : Resveratrol and exercise appear to act through partially distinct mechanisms that combine to produce superior anti-inflammatory and functional outcomes after SCI, supporting their combined use as an adjunct, non-pharmacological rehabilitative strategy. raw.abstractText: Although wood extractives may play important roles in defense against pathogens, few studies have explored the genetic determinism of their accumulation. In this work, we have used a non-targeted metabolomic approach to perform a genetic analysis of grapevine (Vitis vinifera) wood extractive composition in a progeny from a cross between Riesling and Gewurztraminer. Metabolic quantitative trait loci (mQTL) analyses of cane and trunk wood extractives revealed a number of mQTLs. Analysis of one of these mQTL has led to the identification of a cluster of six UDP glycosyltransferase (UGT) genes linked to the accumulation of resveratrol-glucoside (piceid) in both canes and trunks. Detailed biochemical and structural characterization of these six UGTs highlighted a surprising functional diversity among this small gene family, as well as one UGT gene as a key determinant of the constitutive accumulation of piceid in lignified grapevine tissues. Molecular evolution analyses showed that the UGTs in this gene cluster were globally under strong purifying selection, suggesting important biological roles of the corresponding proteins. Moreover, the functional characterization showed that distinct UGT genes were involved in the biosynthesis of cis- and trans- isomers of piceid, suggesting that these isomers may play different biological roles in grapevine.

raw.abstractText: The copper(II)-proline-L-tyrosine and copper(II)-proline-D-tyrosine complex ions, denoted as LL and LD, play an important role in chiral ligand-exchange chromatography (CLEC). These singly charged complexes, containing one neutral and one anionic amino acid ligand, have been isolated in a cryogenic ion trap and characterised by laser spectroscopy in the 3 µm and fingerprint regions. The two diastereomers can be clearly differentiated by their vibrational spectra. Two different isomers for LL and three for LD are deduced from IR-IR hole burning spectra. Quantum chemical calculations show that LL and LD both exist in two square planar structures involving deprotonation of Tyr for one of them or Pro for the other. Although similar in nature, the corresponding LL and LD structures differ by the relative position of the Tyr aromatic ring and the Pro ring, which are on the same side of the N/O⋯Cu⋯N/O plane for LL and on opposite sides for LD. They also differ by the puckering state, endo or exo, of the proline ring. In addition, the LD complex stands out by the presence of a kinetically trapped structure that contains Pro in its zwitterion form, with a very characteristic spectroscopic signature. This finding confirms the role of zwitterionic structures in the chemistry of copper clusters of amino acids.

papers.title: Amino Acid Remodeling Precedes Malignant Transformation in Oral Epithelial Cells

raw.title: Amino Acid Remodeling Precedes Malignant Transformation in Oral Epithelial Cells
raw.authorString: Das K, Haldavanekar S, Ishwar D.
raw.abstractText:
Background:

The accessibility of the oral cavity and the presence of clinically identifiable oral potentially malignant disorders provide an important opportunity for oral cancer prevention. However, current clinical and histopathological assessments cannot reliably predict which lesions will undergo malignant transformation. Here, we investigated amino acid alterations and related proteomic remodeling that characterize potentially malignant oral epithelial cells relative to healthy and malignant cells. Methods Healthy, potentially malignant, and malignant oral epithelial cell models were analyzed using Raman spectroscopy and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based proteomics. Raman spectral profiles were compared across the three states of epithelial transformation, focusing on aromatic amino acid-associated spectral regions. Proteomic changes were evaluated using differential abundance and pathway analyses, and the potentially malignant remodeling patterns were integrated with Raman findings. Results Raman spectroscopy identified distinct biochemical profiles across the three cellular states, with prominent alterations in the 1000-1165 cm-1 region. Phenylalanine-associated features near 1001-1004 cm-1 were increased in the potentially malignant state and subsequently decreased in malignant cells. In contrast, tyrosine-associated bands near 1164 cm-1 were reduced in potentially malignant cells and increased in malignant cells. Proteomic analysis identified extensive stage-associated remodeling of amino acid metabolism, transport, and protein synthesis. Early alterations included changes in GOT1, GOT2, GPT2, IVD, HIBCH, DBT, DLD, ALDH6A1, ALDH4A1, SHMT1, CTH, and other amino acid-associated proteins. Integration of the datasets identified convergence between aromatic amino acid-associated Raman features and early proteomic remodeling. Conclusions Potentially malignant oral epithelial cells exhibited distinct Raman and proteomic signatures that differentiated them from both healthy and malignant cells. The correspondence between aromatic amino acid-associated Raman features and changes in proteins involved in amino acid metabolism and transport supports the presence of a distinct biochemical state associated with potential malignancy. These findings identify candidate molecular features for further validation in patient-derived lesions and future studies of malignant transformation risk.

papers.title: Dynamical consequences of context-dependent mutation: visualizing antibody sequence evolution during somatic hypermutation

raw.title: Dynamical consequences of context-dependent mutation: visualizing antibody sequence evolution during somatic hypermutation
raw.authorString: Kovaleva VA, Meyer HV, McCandlish DM.
raw.abstractText: Context-dependent mutation models describe how local sequence context affects individual substitution rates, but how these biases shape sequence evolution over multiple mutational steps remains challenging to characterize. Here, we develop a framework for analyzing and visualizing long-term sequence dynamics arising from context-dependent, non-reversible mutation processes. We apply it to somatic hypermutation during antibody affinity maturation, using previously inferred context-dependent mutation rates. Our analysis recovers conventional hypermutation hot- and cold-spot patterns while exposing substantial heterogeneity in mutability within these categories. We also identify sequences with low mutability that lack conventional cold-spot motifs. Applying the framework to antigen-binding regions from different antibody-encoding gene families reveals how differences in sequence composition lead to distinct mutational trajectories through sequence space, suggesting that hypermutation biases constrain how these regions diversify. We further show how mutational biases defined at the level of 5-nucleotide contexts propagate to the codon and amino acid levels, producing low stationary frequencies for stop codons and tyrosine and high stationary frequencies for proline. Changes in amino acid composition between naive and memory B cells are qualitatively consistent with these predictions. Together, our results provide a general framework for connecting local context-dependent mutation rates to long-term sequence evolution and demonstrate how intrinsic somatic hypermutation biases shape the relative accessibility of different regions of sequence space during affinity maturation.

evidenceQuotes: The combined resveratrol + exercise group showed the most consistent anti-inflammatory profile, with significantly lower IL-6 than the exercise-alone group, and was the only intervention group with significantly reduced TNF-α. BBB scores improved significantly only in the exercise-containing groups.

payload.caution: Evidence is from a controlled experimental study in male Wistar rats with spinal cord injury; applicability to humans is not established by this abstract.

proposals.rationale: The reported findings are preclinical and model-specific, so they should not be generalized directly to human spinal cord injury or clinical treatment.
evidenceQuotes: Controlled experimental animal study.

payload.effect: Tyrosine-associated Raman bands near 1164 cm-1 were reduced in potentially malignant oral epithelial cells and increased in malignant oral epithelial cells.
payload.model: Healthy, potentially malignant, and malignant oral epithelial cell models

proposals.rationale: The abstract reports a stage-associated change in a tyrosine-associated Raman feature across oral epithelial cell transformation states, supporting a new observational effect for tyrosine-related biochemical signatures.
evidenceQuotes: In contrast, tyrosine-associated bands near 1164 cm-1 were reduced in potentially malignant cells and increased in malignant cells.
